target_customer: Engineering teams building products that combine hardware and software, such as robotics, defense and embedded systems
problem: Hardware and software workflows are separate, so integration failures are hard to trace and fixes are hard to verify on real hardware.
business_model: B2B enterprise software subscription (inferred, pricing not found)
product_category: Agentic engineering platform for hardware and software co-development

founders.name: Justin Leong
education: Stanford, MS and BS in Computer Science
founders.background_notes: YC page says he worked on Roadrunner GNC firmware at Anduril.

founders.background_notes: Surname not available. Launch coverage names him as a founder; the team is described as Stanford CS and physics engineers with Anduril and OpenAI experience.

competitors.name: BootLoop
competitors.what: AI agent for firmware and hardware-in-the-loop testing
competitors.traction_then: Launched BootLoop Test on 2026-06-01; no named customers found

competitors.name: Embedder
competitors.what: AI coding agent for embedded firmware that compiles, flashes and tests on target hardware
competitors.traction_then: Nominated for Embedded Award 2026 startup category

technical_complexity.rationale: Must tie repositories, hardware interfaces and test evidence into a system graph and run agents against real hardware benches, which needs integration with varied test stacks.

defensibility.rationale: Several startups attack embedded and firmware agents; the moat would be integrations with customer benches and accumulated system graphs.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: General coding agents are the baseline HyperBench benchmarks against; no incumbent action on hardware-in-the-loop was found.

market_need_then: Coding agents made software writing cheaper, shifting the bottleneck to integration and hardware verification. Evidence is the company's own claim of 20% higher correctness than vanilla Claude and Codex on a system-level benchmark.

identity.visual_style: Dark and minimal with partner logos
identity.voice_and_tone: Direct, concise, verb section labels such as Understand, Reproduce, Repair, Verify

branding.brand_signature: Tagline: Hardware and software. Developed together.

brand_strength.rationale: Clear tagline but the name collides with an academic HyperBench benchmark and many Hyper-prefixed companies; little brand press found.

outcome_analysis: HyperBench is a two-person Fall 2026 company with founders from Anduril and OpenAI-linked backgrounds that has just launched its platform. No funding round, exit or distress was found, so the outcome is too early to assess. The main risk is the growing set of embedded AI agent startups and general coding agents.
notes: Founded year not found. Co-founder Ivan G. appears only in one outlet and the YC page does not name him; the YC page links an unnamed second founder. Competitor dates are for launches near the batch (summer 2026). A Fall 2026 batch listing was not independently confirmed by search. Benchmark claim is self-reported.
